planning_note: Organise around FSM with three explicit states, support logic, and output updates. All functional blocks (debounce, synchronisers, command assembly, status processing, watchdog) must be represented as distinct structural regions for retrieval purposes.

structural_blocks.purpose: Declare all internal storage, synchroniser stages, next-state combination signals, and locally used constants.
must_appear: synchroniser stages for req_in and ack_in
output register objects for settings, cmd_out, RESP_1_REG, STATUS_REG, interrupt registers
retrieval_focus: all synchronous objects required by spec

structural_blocks.purpose: Pure combinational logic to compute next state of the FSM based on current state, New_CMD, ack_in_int, and complete.
must_appear: default return to IDLE for unlisted conditions
full sensitivity to state, New_CMD, ack_in_int, complete
retrieval_focus: transition conditions exactly as in spec

structural_blocks.purpose: Register the current state on posedge CLK_PAD_IO or asynchronous reset, resetting to IDLE.
retrieval_focus: state register update exactly as per timing contract

structural_blocks.purpose: Combinational logic used during SETUP to generate next_cmd_out and next_settings values from CMD_SET_REG, ARG_REG, data_read/data_write, and response_size.
structural_blocks.code_shape: combinational block computing next_cmd_out, next_settings, and response_size
must_appear: assembly of 16-bit settings according to bit mapping
retrieval_focus: exact bit-level mapping as in spec

structural_blocks.purpose: Sequential debounce of card_detect signal; updates debounce counter and card_present flag on posedge CLK_PAD_IO or reset.
structural_blocks.code_shape: sequential block with asynchronous reset and counter logic
must_appear: debounce counter reaching 15 to set card_present

structural_blocks.purpose: Two-stage synchronisation of asynchronous req_in and ack_in inputs to generate req_in_int and ack_in_int.
structural_blocks.code_shape: sequential block with asynchronous reset, two flip-flop stages per signal

structural_blocks.purpose: Main sequential block that updates per-state outputs, control signals, watchdog, status, response, and interrupts on posedge CLK_PAD_IO or reset.
structural_blocks.code_shape: sequential block with asynchronous reset, state-machine style case on state
must_appear: registered outputs for cmd_out and settings loaded only in SETUP
watchdog counter increment and timeout in EXECUTE
interrupt/status updates according to spec tables
card_present reflected in NORMAL_INT_REG bit assignments (bits 1,2)
retrieval_focus: exact state-dependent operations as detailed in spec

semantic_modes.meaning: awaiting new command, monitoring serial status
assembling command and settings, clearing interrupt registers, enabling checks, resetting watchdog
transmitting command, managing handshake, processing responses, watchdog timeout enforcement

state_model.notes: driven by next‑state combinational logic, reset to IDLE

global_invariants: cmd_out and settings outputs stable once set in SETUP and held through EXECUTE until next command
interrupt registers reflect the last known error/completion until explicitly cleared
open_semantic_questions: exact pulse width of req_out/ack_out handshake is not fully defined; may be edge‑driven or held
complete signal precise timing (level vs pulse) not specified

responsibilities: provide all shared declared objects needed by other blocks
timing_semantics: purely declarative, no active timing constraints
touched_objects: all registers, wires, combinational intermediates declared in B1
coupling_rules: every downstream block must reference objects declared here
forbidden_drift: do not pre‑assign functional role to any declared object beyond its spec‑defined purpose

timing_semantics: zero‑delay combinational path from state and inputs to next_state
coupling_rules: drives next_state used by B3; must respond to combinational changes instantly
forbidden_drift: do not embed registered elements or side‑effects

timing_semantics: synchronous positive‑edge update, asynchronous active‑high reset
coupling_rules: only source of state register update; consumes next_state from B2
forbidden_drift: do not modify state to anything other than IDLE on reset

timing_semantics: combinational output valid after inputs (CMD_SET_REG, ARG_REG, data_read, data_write) settle
touched_objects: next_cmd_out, next_settings, response_size, CMD_SET_REG, ARG_REG, data_read, data_write
coupling_rules: results sampled only during SETUP in B7
forbidden_drift: do not infer registered storage inside this block

timing_semantics: updates debounce counter and card_present on each clock edge
coupling_rules: card_present is used by B7 for NORMAL_INT_REG assignment; block operates independently of FSM state
forbidden_drift: do not interfere with FSM or handshake logic

responsibilities: synchronise req_in and ack_in to internal clock domain
timing_semantics: two‑stage flip‑flop synchronisation; updates on each posedge
coupling_rules: req_in_int and ack_in_int used by B2 and B7; block independent of FSM state
forbidden_drift: do not add extra pipelining beyond two stages

responsibilities: execute all state‑dependent outputs, control signal updates, watchdog, interrupt and status management, response capture
timing_semantics: sequential updates on posedge; defaults assigned then overwritten per state
touched_objects: cmd_out_reg, settings_reg, RESP_1_REG, STATUS_REG, NORMAL_INT_REG, ERR_INT_REG, complete, CRC_check_enable, index_check_enable, go_idle_o, req_out, ack_out, CICMD, Watchdog_Cnt
coupling_rules: consumes card_present (from B5), next_cmd_out/next_settings (from B4), req_in_int/ack_in_int (from B6), state (from B3)
forbidden_drift: do not duplicate debounce, synchroniser, or next‑state logic
do not invent new states or output ports

chosen_decisions.decision: Separate combinational next‑state, combinational output assembly, and sequential blocks for state register, debounce, synchronisers, and main per‑state operations. This mirrors the distinct functional blocks in the spec and simplifies later retrieval and change.
chosen_decisions.reason: Spec explicitly describes these as separate functions; separation minimises block coupling and isolates timing concerns.

deferred_decisions: exact encoding of `response_size` constants (small_rsp, big_rsp) and their bit patterns – left to code generation
precise handshake cycle behaviour (req_out/ack_out/req_in/ack_in) is not fully specified; block B7 must remain flexible to implement edge‑based or level‑based protocol as clarified later
encoding of `complete` (registered pulse vs level) – deferred until timing closure
structural_risks: Block B7 may become monolithic if state operations grow; future refactoring into per‑state sub‑blocks may be needed, but currently not justified.
Combinational block B4 may need to be combined with B7 if registered outputs require combinational path synchronous to latch, but current split preserves clarity.
behavioral_risks: Asynchronous reset timing and removal synchronisation not specified; actual implementation may need reset synchroniser.
Debounce threshold of 15 clocks is hard‑coded; any requirement to change it would touch block B5.
